sources.title: Andrea Kay and colleagues, Diversification, Intensification and Specialization: Changing Land Use in Western Africa from 1800 BC to AD 1500 (2019)
sources.note: Full original synthesis read directly. Abstract, regional time windows and AD 1500 rice-coast discussion. Same work as DOI and UCL Fuller_Kay2019_Article_DiversificationIntensification.pdf. Public overview distinguishes author research from defective imported geometry; no implication this article authored the imported polygons.

sources.title: Dorian Fuller and colleagues, Transition From Wild to Domesticated Pearl Millet Revealed in Ceramic Temper at Three Middle Holocene Sites in Northern Mali (2021)
sources.note: Full primary archaeobotanical study directly read. Methods, figures 5 to 8 and discussion trace domestication traits from grain/chaff impressions. Specific analysed northern Mali sites predate imported 1500 BCE start; use explicitly as earlier background, not invented contemporary event.

sources.title: Kevin MacDonald and colleagues, Dhar Néma: from early agriculture to metallurgy in southeastern Mauritania (2009)
sources.note: Original author-uploaded paper read directly. Survey inventory, Bou Khzama II discussion and figures 11 to 12 distinguish low cobble platforms from schist pillar groups. Proposed granary and drying-rack functions are analogical interpretations, not surviving organic superstructures. Many surface features span Late Tichitt/Historic phases and cannot be assigned one precise year.

sources.title: Louis Champion and colleagues, A question of rite: pearl millet consumption at Nok culture sites, Nigeria (2023)
sources.note: Full original research directly read. Abstract, methods and discussion; more than 11000 remains from 50 sites, 9220 millet grains, no chaff despite fine sieving. Feasting at ritual consumer sites is proposed, not proven for every Nok context. Original online publication 2022, journal volume 2023.

sources.title: Julie Dunne and colleagues, Honey-collecting in prehistoric West Africa from 3500 years ago (2021)
sources.note: Primary chemical residue study, full indexed publisher text checked. 458 sherds from 12 Nok sites, beeswax in over one-third of lipid-yielding samples. Bee-product processing direct; honey collection likely; no transfer of modern Okiek meat-preserving custom to Nok.

sources.title: Champion and colleagues, Agricultural diversification in West Africa: an archaeobotanical study of the site of Sadia (2021)
sources.note: Full indexed original article checked, reinforced by UCL abstract https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10124799/ and publisher DOI 10.1007/s12520-021-01293-5. Direct PMC challenge. Occupation about 750 to 1300 CE; phase 1 eighth to ninth, phase 2 tenth to eleventh, phase 3 twelfth to late thirteenth century. Crop diversification interpreted as risk buffering; tree fruit remains do not prove planted orchards.

sources.title: Mamma Haidara Commemorative Library, Book of the Blessed Merits of Crafts and Agriculture, Library of Congress 2021667257
sources.note: Original manuscript digitization and catalogue. Catalogue obtained via public JSON endpoint, stored agriculture-catalogue.json. Original 64-page PDF downloaded from catalogue resource https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdcwdl/wd/l_/09/66/9/wdl_09669/wdl_09669.pdf . First page rendered locally and visually read; red heading contains فضل الحرث والزرع . Normalized modern Arabic transcription, no manuscript diacritics copied. English translation by drafting researcher: merits of tillage and planting. Catalogue dates copy broadly 1500 to 1900; anonymous authorship, no exact year or author origin supplied. Title in catalogue devised in English.

proposedOverrides.name: West African cereal farmers
proposedOverrides.summary: Distinct West African farming societies and their varied crops, food preparation and agricultural knowledge.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Imported broad food-production label, not a state or ethnicity. Decoded bounds extend to eastern Somalia. Exact polygon checks place central Nok sample region inside, but Dhar Néma, Sadia and Timbuktu outside in all 26 features. Public text labels outside-outline examples and overview rejects cultural-boundary precision. Earlier domestication evidence explicitly before map; manuscript copy dated broadly 1500 to 1900 and mostly potentially later, never assigned to 1500 or 1530 as point event.
